headline: Tariff costs and a lapsed tax benefit compress profit
summary_short: AGCO's Q2 2026 net sales were $2,609.7M, down 1.0% y/y, as income from operations fell 14.2% to $140.7M on tariff-related costs and lower production volumes; net income attributable to AGCO dropped 75.5% y/y to $77.2M ($1.08 diluted EPS), largely because the year-ago quarter included a one-time $255.2M tax benefit.
summary_long: Net sales fell 1.0% y/y to $2,609.7M as lower EME/Latin America/APA volumes outweighed North America growth and favorable FX. Gross margin slipped to 24.7% from 25.0% on lower production; operating income fell 14.2% to $140.7M on tariffs, lower volumes and higher SG&A/engineering spend, partly offset by IEEPA tariff refunds. Net income fell 75.5% to $77.2M ($1.08 diluted EPS), largely because the year-ago quarter included a one-time $255.2M tax benefit from a legal-entity reorganization. Cash fell to $573.4M and long-term debt to $2,639.5M; AGCO sold its NA Finance JV stakes to Rabobank for $188.4M and repurchased $345.1M of stock. 2026 outlook: modestly higher full-year net sales, margins pressured by tariffs.

drivers.explanation: Net sales fell 1.0% y/y on lower volumes in EME, Latin America and Asia/Pacific/Africa (mainly tractors and implements), partly offset by higher North America volumes and favorable currency translation.
Gross margin fell to 24.7% of net sales from 25.0% a year ago, which the filing attributes to lower production volumes company-wide.
Income from operations fell 14.2% on lower sales/production volumes, higher tariff-related costs, SG&A and engineering expenses, partly offset by IEEPA tariff refunds recognized this quarter.
EBIT rose even as operating income fell because 'Other expense, net' dropped to $15.5M from $48.9M on smaller FX losses, more than offsetting the operating-income decline.
Same swing as EBIT: the sharp drop in other-expense/FX losses more than offset lower operating income, lifting EBITDA despite weaker underlying operations.
The decline is largely a tax-base effect: the year-ago quarter's tax provision included a one-time $255.2M net benefit from a legal-entity reorganization, versus a $40.4M provision this quarter.
EPS fell in line with the net-income decline; share count was down modestly y/y on buybacks, only partly offsetting the drop.
Diluted EPS tracked the net-income decline; diluted shares fell to 71.2M from 74.6M on buybacks, only partly offsetting the drop.
Cash fell as H1 financing outflows ($347.0M of buybacks, $42.0M dividends) and negative operating cash flow outweighed the $188.4M NA Finance JV sale proceeds in investing activities.
Total funded debt of $2,639.5M reflects new Credit Facility borrowings ($290.0M) offset by scheduled repayments across EIB term loans and senior term loans versus the year-ago balance.
Equity fell as $347.0M of share repurchases and dividends paid over the year exceeded net income accretion, per the equity roll-forward.

Net sales were roughly flat y/y with margin/profit compression from tariffs, lower volumes and higher SG&A/engineering spend; the outsized net-income and EPS declines mainly reflect a one-time $255.2M tax benefit in the year-ago quarter that did not repeat.
